occurrenceRemarks: Old record from long before the days of mainland captive releases.
Orange-bellied Parrot perched atop a bush
I have now been informed that this is probably a Blue-winged parrot

Three first-year birds that were banded as juveniles in Tasmania (probably captive-bred and then released, but not certain) and migrated north to Werribee for the winter, but had not (yet?) returned south to Tasmania.

Managed to spot three thanks to a group of bird watchers, photographers and researchers at WTP Not the best photo but good to see them wild and in their natural environment. I was told only 86 are in the wild at this stage.
Unbanded male.
Juvenile orange bellied parrot INAT didn’t come up to ID
3 individuals
Four individuals sighted.

Welp, today was a very lucky day. The individual wandered out on a reed and stayed 8-9 meters in front of me for roughly 45 seconds. Then flew off with 2 other individuals so a total of 3 individuals observed. Snapped about 40 photos with a heartrate of 160bpm.
Utterly joyous moment. 1x Individual. Leg bands reported.
